lede.off: P2P is off. Choose a mode to use other instances or to share this one.
lede.connect: Connect only: this server uses remotes over P2P and accepts nobody.
lede.share: Connect and share: this server also accepts the devices you pair.

loadError: Could not load the P2P settings
saved: Saved. P2P restarts with the new setting.
saveFailed: The server did not save the setting.

off.title: Off
off.body: No P2P. Nodes on NATS and WebSocket are not affected.

connect.title: Connect only
connect.body: Use the models of other instances over P2P. This server accepts nobody. No authentication needed.

share.title: Connect and share
share.body: Also accept paired devices, remotes and P2P nodes. Needs authentication on.

network.title: Network

mode.title: P2P mode
mode.lede: What this instance does over P2P. A change applies at once.

network.shareOnlyNote: Shown only in Connect and share: Share this instance, Devices and invites, Relay for paired devices and Relays.

dht.title: Public DHT
dht.desc: Find and be found through the public libp2p network. Joining never needs it: an invite carries the peer ID and the relay hint, and the client dials the peer ID.

mdns.title: Local network discovery
mdns.desc: Find other instances on the same local network (mDNS), so they connect directly without the internet.

bootstrap.title: Bootstrap peers
bootstrap.desc: Your own entry points to the libp2p network, one address per line. Each address ends in /p2p/<peer ID>. Leave it empty to use the public bootstrap peers.

relayPaired.title: Relay for paired devices
relayPaired.desc: This server carries traffic between its own paired devices when they cannot connect directly. Shown as Via your server.

relayMode.title: When this server relays
relayMode.desc: Automatic runs the relay only while other peers can reach this server from the internet.
relayMode.auto: Automatic: when this server is reachable

relayRate.title: Bandwidth per circuit
relayRate.desc: The limit for each connection this server relays. 0 means no limit.

share.title: Share this instance from here
share.body: Let your laptop use the models of this server, and add P2P nodes. Every device that pairs gets its own API key, so sharing needs authentication on.
share.authOn: Authentication is on. Switching adds Devices and invites, Share this instance and Relays. Your remotes stay connected.

relays.title: Relays
relays.lede: LocalAI runs no public relays. Public libp2p relays coordinate hole punching and carry pairing and small requests; they reset a connection after about 128 KiB. Some pairs of networks cannot connect directly, so run your own relay. A gated relay admits only the peers this server has paired. An open relay can be used in invites, with a warning.

reason.not_public: Waiting: not reachable from the internet

relays.synced: The relay has the current list of paired devices.

empty.title: No relay of your own yet
empty.body: Devices behind strict routers cannot connect directly. A small relay on a machine with a public address gets them in.

outOfSync.title: {{name}} is out of sync.
outOfSync.body_one: It may still admit a device you revoked. Sync now pushes the current list of {{count}} paired device.
outOfSync.body_other: It may still admit a device you revoked. Sync now pushes the current list of {{count}} paired devices.

relays.claimLede: The relay has no admin yet. It printed a one-time claim code when it started.
relays.claimed: This server is now the admin of the relay.
relays.removeBody: {{name}} is not used in new invites any more. The relay keeps running; stop it on its machine.

run.title: Run a relay
run.lede: For peers that cannot connect directly. It admits only the peers this server has paired.
run.step1: 1. Start it on a machine with a public address
run.binaryLabel: Start the relay with the local-ai binary
run.explain: Open UDP and TCP port 4001. The volume keeps the relay key, so its peer ID survives restarts. --admin names this server: the relay admits only the peers this server has paired, and this server updates that list when you pair or revoke a device. Two servers can share one relay: add one --admin for each. The relay is a separate small image, localai/relay. Limits per circuit: --circuit-max-bytes, --circuit-max-duration, --rate-limit, --max-circuits-per-peer. With --open anyone may use it, and it starts at 64 KiB/s per circuit.
run.addrHint: The relay prints its address when it starts.
run.addrInvalid: Paste the full address. It starts with / and ends in /p2p/ and the peer ID of the relay.
run.claimFailed: The relay refused the claim code: {{error}}
run.added: Relay added. New invites name it.
run.nothingSaved: Nothing is saved until you add the relay.

reserve.waiting: Reserve a slot on the relay
reserve.ok: Reserved a slot on the relay

circuit.ok: Circuit test: data went through the relay
circuit.skipped: Circuit test: skipped, this server is not admin

allowlist.ok: Allowlist pushed. This server is admin.
allowlist.skipped: Allowlist: not needed for an open relay

ok.title: The relay works and is gated.
ok.body: It goes into every new invite as the relay hint, with a relay pass.

open.title: The relay works, but it is open.
open.body: Anyone can use it. Invites name it only with a warning. Start it with --admin to make it gated.

wrong_peer.title: Wrong peer ID.
wrong_peer.body: The relay answered as {{actual}}, but the address says {{expected}}. Copy the address again from the relay log. If the relay restarted without its key volume, it made a new ID.

unreachable.title: Cannot reach the relay.
unreachable.body: Check that it runs and that UDP and TCP port 4001 are open on its machine and its router. Then check again.

circuit.title: The relay answers, but no data went through it.
circuit.body: Its limits may be too low, or it is overloaded. Check its log, then check again.

unclaimed.title: The relay has no admin yet.
unclaimed.body: Enter the claim code it printed when it started, or start it again with --admin and the peer ID of this server.

not_admin.title: This server is not an admin of the relay.
not_admin.body: Start the relay with --admin and the peer ID of this server, as in step 1. Then check again.

limits.title: Limits for {{name}}
limits.ledeOpen: Open relay: anyone can use it.
limits.ledeGated: Gated relay: only paired peers use it.
limits.noLimitOpen: One stranger can use all the bandwidth and data of this relay, and your own peers slow down.
limits.noLimitGated: A paired peer can use all the bandwidth of this relay, for example for a model copy.
limits.zeroHint: 0 means no limit for that value.
limits.invalid: Each value must be a number of 0 or more.
limits.applyHint: A new bandwidth limit applies to the next circuit. A new data or time limit restarts the relay's circuit service: circuits that are open keep the old limits until they close, and paired devices reconnect through the relay within moments.
limits.savedRestarted: Limits saved on {{name}}. The relay restarted its circuit service; devices reconnect in a moment.
limits.loadError: Could not read the limits from the relay.
limits.readOnlyTitle: This server cannot change these limits.
limits.readOnlyOpen: This is an open relay and this server is not its admin. Set the limits where the relay runs, with --circuit-max-bytes, --circuit-max-duration and --rate-limit.
limits.readOnlyMember: This server is not an admin of this relay. Ask its admin, or set the limits where the relay runs, with --circuit-max-bytes, --circuit-max-duration and --rate-limit.
limits.ceilingBody: The operator of this relay set an upper bound for each limit with its start flags. You can change a limit up to its maximum, not above it, and you cannot remove a limit that has a maximum.

issue.required: Enter a value up to {{max}}: a limit with a maximum cannot be removed.

identity.title: Identity
identity.lede: Clients pin this peer ID when they redeem an invite. Your relays name it as their admin. It stays the same across restarts.
identity.notRunning: P2P does not run, so this server has no peer ID to show.
identity.copyFailed: Could not copy the peer ID.
identity.regenerateDesc: Makes a new identity key. The old key is kept as a backup next to the new one. Do this only if the identity key leaked.
identity.regenerated: New peer ID made. Send each device and remote a new invite.
identity.confirmBody: Every paired device, remote and P2P worker pinned the current ID. They stop connecting and refuse the new ID as a security warning. You must send each of them a new invite. Pending invites stop working.
identity.confirmOnly: Do this only if the identity key leaked.
identity.confirmCheck_one: I understand that {{count}} paired device must pair again
identity.confirmCheck_other: I understand that {{count}} paired devices must pair again
